result.document_summary: Massachusetts G.L. c. 151B § 4 (part 1 of 2), the state anti-discrimination statute listing unlawful practices in employment, housing, credit and related areas.
result.notes: One in-scope rule found: subsection 10 bars discrimination against recipients of public assistance or housing subsidies in rental accommodations, which is a source-of-income screening restriction. Employment, credit, commercial space, disability-accommodation and other discrimination provisions are outside the six categories and were ignored. Effective date is not given in this text.

rules.title: Ban on discrimination against recipients of public assistance and housing subsidies
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for any person furnishing rental accommodations to discriminate against an individual because the individual receives federal, state or local public assistance or a housing subsidy (including rental assistance or supplements), or because of any requirement of such a program.
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies
rules.coverage_text: Applies to any person furnishing rental accommodations in Massachusetts, with no unit-count or building-age test stated in this subsection.
